axes.note: Twelve clients, same URL, different data and different requirements per client. This is a discovery dimension, not a parameter — no amount of endpoint enumeration finds it, because the path is identical and only context.client differs.

gates.name: proof-of-origin token
gates.note: Required per client per context, not globally: web_safari HLS needs none, web does, android_vr has no restriction, tv is DRM throughout. Missing where required gives HTTP 403 or an IP/account block.

gates.name: visitorData
gates.note: From the VISITOR_INFO1_LIVE cookie. A value minted by a bare POST returns UNPLAYABLE — it has to come from a browser that navigated the specific watch page.

gates.name: signature / n-sig
gates.note: Format URLs carry a signature descrambled by running a function out of the player JS, keyed by player version as signature_timestamp@hash. Computation, not extraction — neither a header to copy nor an endpoint to call.

gates.name: CPN (content playback nonce)
gates.note: A random 16-character value the client generates itself and sends with playback requests. Not harvested from a response and not computed from anything — the client makes it up and the server expects one. A route that omits it fails for a reason that looks nothing like the cause.

gates.name: BotGuard PoToken
gates.note: Minted through an obfuscated challenge at api/jnn/v1/GenerateIT. Required for adaptive HD formats; not attempted by any run.

redundantPaths.note: The same records are reachable four ways: the initial webpage, the client configs, the JS player, and the InnerTube API — yt-dlp exposes skipping any of them for that reason. Which path a route is built on decides how fragile it is, and an elimination table that only asks which transports exist never surfaces the choice.

breadthPass.method: Instrumented, swept each page type, drained after each so the event buffer could not cap.
breadthPass.note: Every target saturated on transport classes by the second pass. Later pages added endpoints within transports already found, never a new class — which is what the saturation rule predicts and is worth knowing before budgeting a run.
